A minimizer of a function of one variable has a flat tangent line
([flat point](calculus.qmd#def-flat-point)),
and the sign of the second derivative tells a minimum from a maximum.
This section extends both facts to a function $f$ of a $p \times 1$ vector $\vx$:
the gradient $\deriv{\vx} f(\vx)$ (@def-vector-derivative) takes the place of the first derivative,
and a $p \times p$ matrix of second partial derivatives takes the place of the second.
Throughout, $\deriv{\vx} f(\vecf{z})$ means the gradient evaluated at $\vx = \vecf{z}$.
